draft.shortGloss: to taste; to try on; to try out
draft.emotion: curious and attentive, sensing the quality or flavour of something
notes: Stem-changing verb (o > ue): pruebo, pruebas, prueba...
Do not confuse with 'intentar', which means 'to attempt' to do an action (e.g., 'intentar aprender').
Normally used reflexively ('probarse') when talking about trying on clothes.

senses.definition: To eat or drink a small amount of something to check its flavour or see if you like it.

examples.text: Voy a probar la sopa para ver si necesita sal.
examples.translation: I am going to taste the soup to see if it needs salt.
examples.emotion: focused and careful, checking the seasoning

senses.definition: Usually reflexive ('probarse'): to put on clothes or shoes to see if they fit or look good.

examples.text: Quiero probarme estos pantalones antes de comprarlos.
examples.translation: I want to try on these trousers before buying them.
examples.emotion: practical and decisive, evaluating the fit

senses.definition: To use or do something to see how well it works or whether you like it.

examples.text: Voy a probar el coche nuevo este fin de semana.
examples.translation: I am going to try out the new car this weekend.
examples.emotion: excited and ready for a new experience

examples.text: Voy a probar la sopa para ver si necesita sal.
